statement.p: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve \sqrt{x+5y}+\sqrt{3xy} = 7 at the point (1, 3).
The slope of the tangent line to the curve at the given point is .

solution.p: Differentiating implicitly with respect to x gives \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x+5y}} + \frac{5}{2 \sqrt{x+5y}} \, \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{3xy}} \left( y + x \, \frac{dy}{dx} \right) = 0, or (multiplying by 2 \sqrt{3xy} \sqrt{x+5y}) 1 \sqrt{3xy} + 5 \sqrt{3xy} \; \frac{dy}{dx} + 3 y \sqrt{x+5y} + 3 x \sqrt{x+5y} \; \frac{dy}{dx} = 0, so \left( 5 \sqrt{3xy} + 3 x \sqrt{x+5y} \right) \, \frac{dy}{dx} = - \left( 1 \sqrt{3xy} + 3 y \sqrt{x+5y} \right), and therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = - \frac {1 \sqrt{3xy} + 3 y \sqrt{x+5y}}{5 \sqrt{3xy} + 3 x \sqrt{x+5y}}. If x = 1 and y = 3, then \sqrt{x+5y} = 4, \sqrt{3xy} = 3, and hence the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point (1, 3) is \frac{dy}{dx} \Bigg|_{(x, y) = (1, 3)} = - \frac {1 \left( 3 \right) + 3 \left( 3 \right) \left( 4 \right)} {5 \left( 3 \right) + 3 \left( 1 \right) \left( 4 \right)} = -{\frac{13}{9}}.
